articles.title: Bitcoin wallet bug let rogue servers steal funds when users tried to speed up payments
articles.snippet: Attackers replaced legitimate transactions with fake ones, then waited for users to approve higher fees. At least one person lost bitcoin before developers patched the flaw.

articles.title: Keystone says website breach exposed hardware wallet buyers’ addresses
articles.snippet: A security researcher warned that the leaked shipping details could expose crypto holders to targeted scams and physical attacks.

articles.title: Bitcoin Wallet Fixes Critical Flaw That Redirected Funds to Attackers
articles.snippet: A confirmed exploit let rogue servers replace Electrum’s pending transactions, tricking users into redirecting Bitcoin to attacker addresses.

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Rewrites Its Security Policy for a World Where AI Finds Bugs in One Prompt
articles.snippet: Developers will now backport fixes and cut releases immediately for flaws flagged as “easily discoverable,” abandoning long embargoes for bugs an attacker can surface with a single AI prompt.

articles.title: Is the Internet Safe Again After the PHP Nightmare? What You Need to Know
articles.snippet: PHP shipped its fix, attackers launched millions of attempts, and governments say no one has broken in yet. Here's what that means for your passwords, your crypto, and your browsing.
